title: Thirdway's HQ | Thirdway
description: Thirdway partners with owners, occupiers, and professional teams to create world-class spaces.

main: After nearly two decades of proving that better offices make for better business, we are in an era of innovation and growth, raising the standard of our workspaces and reinforcing our position as a market leader. That evolution has now culminated in the creation of our new home at 224 St John Street in the heart of Clerkenwell.

At Thirdway we partner with occupiers, owners, and professional teams to deliver world-class spaces, united by an overarching ambition to facilitate creation and inspire confidence. For us, excellence means pairing market-leading design with exceptional delivery that embeds confidence at every stage of a project.

In transforming our new headquarters, we have delivered the architecture, design & build, branding, furniture and technology throughout. A true testament to the 'Third-way' of how we do things, the scheme showcases the strength of the wider Thirdway Group, bringing together creative, technical, sustainability and delivery expertise to realise a headquarters that embodies its design philosophy: a ‘home for the office’ — a place which speaks to creation and confidence, without compromise.

main: The ambitious refurbishment reinstated a contextually appropriate, materially rich façade and reconfigured the interior across five floors. Acquired in an unoccupied state, the property gave us the opportunity to reshape the entire space without the wasteful removal of an existing fit-out. Originally a factory, 224–232 St John Street was refurbished in the late 1980s with a curtain wall façade and white render. This has now been replaced with a contemporary façade inspired by the building's warehouse heritage, reconnecting it with its historic character while complementing the surrounding Grade II listed buildings.

main: The office needs a home. Not a showroom, but showcasing what an office should look like.

The design is driven by one key priority: the user experience. Retaining the original front and rear staircases, we introduced a striking new central staircase by cutting through the building's centre—a significant technical undertaking. Beginning with a sculptural curved stair in reception, this intervention improves circulation and strengthens visual and physical connections between the five floors, encouraging movement and interaction. Each floor includes its own tea point, meeting rooms and call pods, while thoughtful space planning balances open-plan workspaces with breakout areas to support different ways of working. Employee wellbeing was also central to the brief, with the ground floor dedicated to a generous social and client hub that forms the heart of the headquarters.

main: We transformed the roof into a vibrant social destination for staff and clients, while also accommodating new M&E plant. Rich planting featuring pollinator-friendly species such as lavender, thyme and rosemary enhances biodiversity, creating a welcoming outdoor environment that supports both wellbeing and sustainability.

The project demonstrates how a heritage building can be transformed into a high-performing, future-ready workplace that places equal emphasis on environmental responsibility, accessibility and wellbeing.

Targeting SKA Gold, Fitwel 2 Star and an EPC A rating, the building has been fully decarbonised through the removal of fossil fuels, the installation of air source heat pumps and an all-electric energy strategy powered by a 100% renewable electricity tariff. Intelligent thermal modelling, optimised heating and cooling zones, demand-led ventilation and one of the largest rainwater harvesting systems of its kind further reduce operational impact, while FSC-certified timber, responsibly sourced materials and the reuse of materials from previous projects support a circular approach to design.

Accessibility was a fundamental consideration throughout, with step-free access integrated from arrival through to every floor, including a bespoke entrance lift, passenger lift and DDA-compliant facilities.  Together, these measures create a workplace that not only performs sustainably but enables people to thrive.

main: Every detail of Thirdway's headquarters reflects both our identity and design expertise. Rich materials, bespoke joinery and a hospitality-inspired approach create a warm, welcoming workplace while demonstrating the quality and creativity we deliver across every project.

The interiors reference the building's industrial heritage through metal detailing, Crittall-style glazing and carefully exposed M&E, all integrated into a refined design language. Brand moments are woven subtly throughout the space, from a light installation that reveals Thirdway's wolf emblem from below, to bespoke floor mosaics in the breakout and passenger lift, inspired by our history and the local area's traditional signage.

The strongest expression of the Thirdway brand is the collection of more than 80 bespoke artworks, all conceived and produced in-house by the Thirdway Creative Team. Inspired by our values and story, the artwork reinforces our all-in-house ethos while giving the workplace a distinct sense of personality. Rather than dominating the interiors, these brand moments complement the material palette and craftsmanship, producing a workplace that feels authentic, memorable and unmistakably Thirdway.

main: A fully equipped gym sits at the rear of the ground floor, complemented by high-quality changing facilities nearby. Their proximity creates a seamless user journey, making it easy for employees to incorporate wellness into their working day while reinforcing our people-first approach.
